AI / Data Science Portfolio & Student Learning Platform

Complete User Guide · Setup · Main pages · Forms · Students & visitors · Adding study materials and projects

Version 1.0 — September 2026

1. Introduction

This guide explains how to install, start and use your portfolio and learning website, what every main page and form does, and how to add your own study materials, projects and other content.

1.1 What the website does

  • Professional portfolio – your profile, skills, experience, certifications and contact details.
  • Resume – an ATS-friendly online resume you can download or print.
  • Project showcase – projects with screenshots, code, architecture diagrams, demos and optional 3D models.
  • Learning platform – study materials, interview questions and timed quizzes, with progress tracking for students.

1.2 Who uses the website

User typeHow they get itWhat they can do
GuestJust opens the websiteBrowse every public page: portfolio, projects, study materials, interview questions, blog. Can take quizzes, but scores are not saved.
Visitor accountRegisters and chooses “Visitor”Everything a guest can do, plus an account page. Can upgrade to a student account at any time.
Student accountRegisters and chooses “Student”Mark lessons complete, bookmark lessons, write private notes, save quiz scores, appear on leaderboards, and use the student dashboard.
Admin (you)Created with the createsuperuser commandEverything above, plus the Admin dashboard and the Content manager where all content is added and edited.

1.3 How the website is built

The website has two parts that run at the same time. You start both of them every time you work on the site.

PartFolderAddress on your computerPurpose
Website (frontend)frontendhttp://localhost:3000The pages your visitors see.
Server (backend)backendhttp://localhost:8000Stores the data, handles logins and serves the API.
Content managerpart of the backendhttp://localhost:8000/django-admin/Where you add and edit projects, lessons and everything else.
Tip: All your content lives in the database, not in the code. You never need to edit code to add a lesson, a project or your personal details.

2. First-time setup (Windows)

2.1 Install the required software

SoftwareNeeded?Where to get itNotes
Python 3.12 or newerYespython.orgAlready installed on this computer (Python 3.14).
Node.js 20.9 or newer (LTS)Yesnodejs.org → download the LTS versionNot installed yet. Keep “Add to PATH” ticked during installation.
PostgreSQLOptionalpostgresql.orgRecommended for going live. The site uses SQLite automatically if PostgreSQL is not set up.
VS CodeRecommendedcode.visualstudio.comTo open the project and use the built-in terminal.

After installing Node.js, close and reopen your terminal, then check both tools work:

python --version
node --version
npm --version

2.2 Set up the backend (server)

Open a terminal in the project folder D:\user\programming\Naveen and run:

cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py seed_demo
CommandWhat it does
python -m venv .venvCreates a private Python environment for the project (only once).
.venv\Scripts\activateSwitches the terminal into that environment. You will see (.venv) at the start of the line. Run this every time you open a new terminal for the backend.
pip install -r requirements.txtInstalls Django and the other backend libraries.
copy .env.example .envCreates your settings file. Skip this if backend\.env already exists.
python manage.py migrateCreates the database tables.
python manage.py seed_demoAdds the 18 study subjects, your skill list and 5 sample projects. Safe to run again.
Already done: On this computer the backend environment, database and sample data are already set up. You only need to create your admin account (next step).

2.3 Create your admin account

With the backend environment active, run:

python manage.py createsuperuser

It asks for your email, full name and a password (typed twice, the characters are hidden). Use a strong password. This account can log in to both the website and the Content manager.

2.4 Backend settings file (backend\.env)

Open backend\.env in a text editor. The most important settings:

SettingExampleMeaning
DEBUGtruetrue while developing on your computer, false on the live server.
SECRET_KEYa long random textSecret used to sign logins. Must be long and private when live.
DATABASE_URLpostgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/portfolioLeave empty to use SQLite. Set it to use PostgreSQL.
FRONTEND_URLhttp://localhost:3000Address of the website; used in password-reset links.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINShttp://localhost:3000Website addresses allowed to talk to the server.
EMAIL_BACKEND + EMAIL_HOST…smtp settingsNeeded to really send password-reset emails. Without it, emails are printed in the backend terminal.
USE_S3 + AWS_…true / bucket detailsStore uploaded files in cloud storage when the site is live.
Important: Never share or upload your .env files. They contain passwords and secret keys.

2.5 Set up the frontend (website)

Open a second terminal in the project folder and run:

cd frontend
npm install
copy .env.example .env.local
Setting (frontend\.env.local)DefaultMeaning
API_URLhttp://localhost:8000/apiWhere the website finds the server.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URLhttp://localhost:3000Public address of the site (used for SEO and sharing links).
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_NAMEMy PortfolioName shown until you fill in your name in the Site profile.
NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_URLhttp://localhost:8000/django-admin/Link used by the “Open content manager” button.

2.6 Start the website (every day)

You need two terminals open at the same time.

Terminal 1 – backend

cd D:\user\programming\Naveen\backend
.venv\Scripts\activate
python manage.py runserver

Terminal 2 – frontend

cd D:\user\programming\Naveen\frontend
npm run dev

Now open http://localhost:3000 in your browser. To stop either part, click in its terminal and press Ctrl + C.

Tip: npm run dev reloads automatically when code changes. To test the fast production version on your computer, run npm run build and then npm start instead.

2.7 Optional: switch to PostgreSQL

  1. Install PostgreSQL and create an empty database, for example portfolio.
  2. In backend\.env set DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/portfolio.
  3. Run python manage.py migrate, then python manage.py seed_demo, then python manage.py createsuperuser again (the new database starts empty).
  4. Restart the backend.

3. Tour of the main pages

3.1 Navigation bar

The bar at the top of every page contains:

  • Logo and name – click to return to the home page. The name comes from your Site profile.
  • Menu links – Home, About, Resume, Skills, Projects, Study Materials, Certifications, Experience, Blog, Contact.
  • Search (magnifying glass) – searches projects, courses, lessons, interview questions, blog posts and certificates. Shortcut: Ctrl + K.
  • Theme button – each click switches Light → Dark → System (follows your computer). The choice is remembered.
  • Login / account circle – shows “Login” when logged out. When logged in it shows your initials; click it for My learning, Admin dashboard, Account settings and Log out.
  • Menu button (☰) – on phones and small screens all links move into this menu. Interview Prep and Practice Quizzes are also listed there.

3.2 Home page

  • Hero section – your name, headline and tagline, with buttons for View Resume, View Projects, Study Materials and Contact Me.
  • Skill badges – the short list under the buttons (edit “Hero badges” in the Site profile).
  • 3D neural network – input, hidden and output layers that follow the mouse. Hover a node to highlight its connections. On devices without 3D support a still picture is shown instead, and animation is reduced for people who turn on “reduce motion”.
  • Counters – number of published projects, certifications, skills and lessons.
  • Featured Projects – projects you tick as “Is featured”.
  • Learn with me – quick links to the study subjects.

3.4 Projects and the project viewer

Visitors can filter by All, Python, ML, AI, Data Science, Django, GenAI and search by title, summary or technology. Each card shows the image, category, short description, technologies and links to GitHub, live demo and details.

A project’s detail page has up to six tabs. A tab only appears when you have filled in its content, so a project never shows empty sections:

TabShows
OverviewProblem statement, objective, dataset, technologies, future improvements
ArchitectureInteractive pipeline diagram (from “Pipeline steps”), system architecture, data flow
CodeImplementation, ML algorithm, model training, code snippets, GitHub link
Demo3D model viewer (rotate, zoom, pan, fullscreen), demo videos, live demo button
ResultsEvaluation, results, screenshots
DocumentationWritten documentation and an embedded PDF with a download button

3.5 Study materials and lessons

Materials are organised as Subject → Course (level) → Lessons. The levels are Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Interview Preparation, Projects and Practice Questions.

  • Left sidebar – every lesson in the course; the current one is highlighted.
  • Content – headings, formatted text, code with colours, tables, images and an optional video.
  • Downloadable notes & resources – files attached to the lesson.
  • Previous Lesson / Next Lesson – buttons at the bottom.
  • Mark as Completed, Bookmark, My notes – for students (see section 5).

3.6 Interview preparation

Open Interview Prep from the phone menu or footer, or go to /interview. Choose a subject, then filter by Easy / Medium / Hard or search. Click a question to open its short answer, detailed answer, example, code and interview tip.

3.7 Practice quizzes

Go to /practice, choose a quiz and press Start Quiz. Answer one question at a time using Previous / Next, then Submit. The timer submits automatically when time runs out. Results show your score, the correct answers and explanations, a Retry button and the leaderboard.

3.8 Resume page

  • Download Resume PDF – appears when you upload a resume PDF in the Site profile.
  • Save as PDF – appears when no PDF is uploaded. It opens the print window; choose “Save as PDF” as the printer.
  • Print Resume – prints a clean black-and-white layout without the menu and buttons.

3.9 Certifications, blog and search

  • Certifications – each card has a Verify Certificate link to /certificate/<credential ID>, which shows the details and a link to the provider’s own verification page. Share that link with employers.
  • Blog – filter by category, search, and read articles with reading time and tags.
  • Search – type at least 2 characters. Results are grouped by type (Projects, Lessons, Blog…).

4. Forms – field by field

4.1 Register (Create your account)

Address: /register. Also reachable from the Login page (“Create a student or visitor account”).

FieldRequiredRules
I am joining as aYesStudent (default) or Visitor. Admin accounts cannot be created here.
Full nameYesAt least 2 characters.
EmailYesValid email address. Each email can only be used once.
PasswordYesAt least 8 characters, not only numbers, not a common password, not too similar to the name or email. Use the eye icon to show/hide.
Confirm passwordYesMust match the password.

After Create student account (or Create visitor account) the person is logged in straight away. Students go to their dashboard; visitors return to the home page.

4.2 Login

FieldRules
EmailThe email used when registering (capital letters don’t matter).
PasswordCase-sensitive.
  • Wrong details show “Invalid email or password.”
  • After 10 attempts in a minute the form asks the person to wait (protection against password guessing).
  • After login: admins → /admin, students → /student, visitors → home. If someone was sent to login from a protected page, they return to that page.
  • “Continue browsing as a guest” goes to Study Materials without logging in.

4.3 Forgot password and Reset password

  1. On the Login page click Forgot password?, enter the email and press Send reset link.
  2. The message is the same whether or not the email exists (so nobody can check which emails are registered).
  3. The email contains a link to /reset-password, valid for 2 hours and usable once.
  4. On that page enter the new password twice and press Set new password. The person is sent to Login.
Important: Until you configure email in backend\.env, reset emails are not sent. They are printed in the backend terminal instead. Copy the link from there to test the flow.

4.4 Account settings

Address: /account (account circle → Account settings).

SectionFieldsNotes
Become a studentUpgrade account buttonVisitors only. Switches the account to Student immediately.
ProfileFull name; Email (read-only); for students also College/Institution, Course of study, Interests, Short bioPress Save profile.
PasswordCurrent password, New passwordThe new password follows the same rules as registration.

4.5 Contact form

FieldRequiredRules
NameYes2–120 characters

Messages appear in the Content manager under Contact → Contact messages, and the unread count shows on your Admin dashboard. Spam protection is built in: a hidden trap field, a minimum time to fill in the form, and a limit of 5 messages per hour per person.

MessageMeaning / what to do

5. Guide for students

  1. Go to /register, choose Student, fill in the form and press Create student account.
  2. Open Study Materials, choose a subject, then a lesson from a level (start with Beginner).
  3. Read the lesson, download any attached notes, and press Mark as Completed when done.
  4. Press Bookmark to save lessons you want to revisit, and use My notes for your own notes.
  5. Use Next Lesson to continue through the course.
  6. Test yourself in Practice quizzes. Your scores are saved and you appear on the leaderboard (first name only).
  7. Prepare for interviews in Interview Prep.
  8. Open My learning (account circle) to see your dashboard.
Dashboard itemMeaning
Lessons CompletedTotal lessons marked complete.
Courses CompletedCourses where every published lesson is complete.
Average Quiz ScoreAverage of saved quiz results.
BookmarksNumber of bookmarked lessons, listed at the bottom.
Learning ProgressOne bar per subject: completed lessons out of total.
Recent ActivityLatest completed lessons and quiz scores, with links.

6. Guide for visitors

  • Guests (no account) can read everything public and take quizzes without saving scores.
  • A Visitor account is for recruiters, employers or people who just want to browse and keep in touch.
  • Visitors who open student-only features see a message offering to upgrade.
  • To upgrade: account circle → Become a student (or Account settings → Upgrade account). All student features unlock immediately.

7. Admin guide – managing your content

7.1 Your two admin areas

AreaAddressUse it for
Admin dashboardhttp://localhost:3000/adminOverview: user counts, quiz attempts, unread messages, published vs total for each content type, Add / Manage shortcuts, newest users.
Content managerhttp://localhost:8000/django-admin/Adding, editing, publishing and deleting all content and users.

Log in to each one separately with the same admin email and password.

7.2 Content manager basics

  • List pages show all items. Use the search box, and the Filter panel on the right (category, published, level…).
  • Some columns (Published, Featured, Order) can be edited straight in the list. Press Save at the bottom of the list afterwards.
  • Add creates a new item. Bold field names are required.
  • Buttons: Save (back to the list), Save and add another, Save and continue editing.
  • Publish / Unpublish: tick items in a list, choose “Publish selected items” or “Unpublish selected items” in the Action menu, press Go.
  • Delete: open the item and press Delete (bottom left), or use the “Delete selected” action.
  • The Slug is the part of the web address (for example python-basics). Leave it empty and it is created from the title.
  • Order controls sorting: smaller numbers appear first.
Important: New projects, courses, lessons, quizzes, questions, certificates and blog posts are hidden until Is published is ticked. If something doesn’t appear on the website, check this box first.
Tip: Pages are cached for speed. After publishing, a change can take up to about 1 minute to appear (5 minutes for your name and profile). Refresh the page.

7.5 Adding study materials (step by step)

The 18 subjects (Python, C, C++, SQL, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Statistics, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Power BI, Excel, Django, FastAPI, Data Science, Generative AI, Agentic AI) already exist. You add courses and lessons inside them.

A. Create a course (a level inside a subject)

  1. Go to Learning → Courses → Add.
  2. Category: choose the subject, e.g. Python.
  3. Title: e.g. Python Basics.
  4. Level: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Interview Preparation, Projects or Practice Questions.
  5. Description (optional) and Order (1, 2, 3…).
  6. Tick Is published and press Save.

B. Add lessons to the course

  1. Go to Learning → Lessons → Add.
  2. Course: choose the course you created.
  3. Title (e.g. Variables) and a one-line Summary.
  4. Content: write the lesson in Markdown (see 7.6). Code blocks, tables and images are supported.
  5. Video url (optional): a YouTube, Vimeo or direct video link.
  6. Estimated minutes (optional) and Order: 1 for the first lesson, 2 for the next… This sets the Previous/Next order.
  7. Study materials section at the bottom: attach PDFs, notes, code files, slides or datasets. Choose the Kind, pick a File or paste an External url.
  8. Tick Is published and press Save.

The lesson appears at /study-materials/<subject>/<lesson>, for example /study-materials/python/variables.

Study material optionMeaning
Is downloadableUntick to list the file without a download link.
Requires loginOnly logged-in users get the download link.
Allowed filesPDF, images, videos, py, ipynb, sql, txt, md, js, ts, c, cpp, java, csv, json, zip, pptx, docx, xlsx (up to 100 MB)
Tip: You can also add lessons quickly from inside a course: open the course and use the Lessons table at the bottom. Attach course-wide files (a full-course PDF, for example) in the course’s Study materials table.

7.6 Markdown cheat sheet

Lesson content, project sections, the About text and blog posts use Markdown:

You typeResult
## HeadingSection heading (use ### for a smaller one)
**bold** *italic*Bold and italic text
- itemBullet list
1. stepNumbered list
[text](https://link)Link
![description](https://image-url)Image
> noteHighlighted quote
```python …your code… ```Code block with colours. First line: three backticks followed by the language (python, sql, javascript…). Then your code. Last line: three backticks. See the example below.
| A | B | / |---|---| / | 1 | 2 |Table (header row, separator row, data rows)

Example lesson content:

## What is a variable?

A variable is a **name** bound to a value.

```python
age = 21
print(age)
```

| Type | Example |
|------|---------|
| int  | 21      |
| str  | "hi"    |

7.7 Adding a project

Go to Projects → Projects → Add. The form is split into sections:

SectionFieldsNotes
CardTitle, Slug, Category, Summary, Cover image, TechnologiesSummary is the short text on the card (max 300 characters). Add technologies with the green + or pick existing ones.
LinksGitHub url, Live demo url, Demo video urlYouTube/Vimeo links are embedded automatically.
OverviewProblem statement, Objective, DatasetMarkdown.
ArchitecturePipeline steps, Architecture, Data flowPipeline steps draw the interactive diagram (format below).
ImplementationImplementation, Machine learning algorithm, Model trainingMarkdown.
ResultsEvaluation, Results, Future improvementsMarkdown; include metrics and tables here.
Documentation & 3DDocumentation, Documentation PDF, Model 3D3D model: GLB (best), GLTF or OBJ, up to 50 MB.
PublishingIs published, Is featured, Is sample, OrderFeatured projects appear on the home page and resume.
Project images / videos / code snippetsTables at the bottomScreenshots with captions, extra videos, and code with a language (python, sql…).

Pipeline steps must be written as a list in square brackets with each step in double quotes:

["Dataset", "Data Cleaning", "EDA", "Feature Engineering", "Train/Test Split", "Model Training", "Evaluation", "Prediction"]
Important: The 5 sample projects are marked Is sample and show a “Sample” badge. Replace their content with your real work, or select them in the list and delete them, so no invented work appears on your portfolio.

Go to Learning → Interview questions → Add.

FieldNotes
CategoryThe subject, e.g. Python. The subject appears on /interview once it has a published question.
Question, Short answerRequired.

7.9 Quizzes

  1. Go to Quizzes → Quizzes → Add.
  2. Fill in Title, Description, Category, Difficulty and Time limit minutes (0 = no limit). Leave Show leaderboard ticked to show top scores.
  3. Add questions in the Quiz questions section at the bottom (use “Add another Quiz question” for more).
  4. Tick Is published and press Save.
Question typeFill inExample
MCQOptions (list) and Correct option (counting from 0)Options ["tuple", "list", "str"], Correct option 1 = list
Output predictionCode, Accepted answersCode print(2 ** 3), Accepted answers ["8"]
SQL / Coding / DebuggingAccepted answers (optional)["SELECT * FROM students;"]; leave [] for self-review
TheoryExplanationNot auto-scored; the explanation is shown after submitting

Every question can have an Explanation (shown in the results) and Points (default 1). Student attempts are listed under Quizzes → Quiz attempts.

FieldNotes

Important: Only add certificates you have actually earned, with their real credential IDs.

7.11 Blog posts

  1. Go to Blog → Blog posts → Add.
  2. Fill in Title, Excerpt (short summary), Content (Markdown) and a Featured image.
  3. Choose a Category (9 were created for you) and add Tags.
  4. Tick Is published. The publish date is set automatically the first time.

7.12 Contact messages

Contact → Contact messages lists every message with the newest first. Tick Is read after dealing with one. Reply by email from your normal email program.

7.13 Managing users

TaskHow
Find a userAccounts → Users; search by email or name, filter by Role.

Reset someone’s passwordOpen the user and use the “this form” link under Password, or ask them to use Forgot password.
See a student’s activityLearning → Progress, Bookmarks; Quizzes → Quiz attempts (filter or search by email).

8. Troubleshooting

ProblemSolution
node or npm is not recognisedInstall Node.js LTS from nodejs.org, then close and reopen the terminal.
python manage.py … fails with “No module named django”Activate the environment first: .venv\Scripts\activate inside the backend folder.
Website shows “coming soon” everywhere or “server is unavailable”The backend is not running. Start Terminal 1 (section 2.6).
New content doesn’t showTick Is published (and publish the course as well as the lesson). Wait up to a minute and refresh.
Name still says “My Portfolio” / “Your Name”Fill in Full name in the Site profile; it updates within 5 minutes.
Can’t log in to the Content managerLog in there separately. The account must be an admin (created with createsuperuser or Role = Admin).
Forgot my admin passwordIn the backend terminal: python manage.py changepassword your@email.com.
Password reset email never arrivesEmail isn’t configured yet; copy the link from the backend terminal, or set EMAIL_… in backend\.env.
“Port 3000/8000 is already in use”The site is already running in another terminal. Close it, or restart your computer.
3D animation doesn’t appearThe browser or device doesn’t support 3D graphics, so the still picture is shown. Update the browser or enable hardware acceleration.
File upload rejectedCheck the file type and size limits (images 10 MB, PDFs 25 MB, videos 200 MB, 3D models 50 MB, study files 100 MB).

9. Putting the website online

The project is prepared for Vercel (website), Render (server and PostgreSQL database) and cloud file storage. Full details are in README.md.

  1. Put the project in a GitHub repository. The .gitignore file already keeps .env files and the local database out.
  2. On Render, create a new Blueprint from the repository. render.yaml creates the server and a PostgreSQL database and generates secret keys.
  3. In Render set FRONTEND_URL, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to your Vercel address, and ALLOWED_HOSTS to the Render address.
  4. Set up an S3 or Cloudflare R2 bucket and set USE_S3=true with the AWS_… keys, so uploaded files are kept permanently.
  5. Configure email (EMAIL_BACKEND, EMAIL_HOST, …) so password-reset emails are delivered.
  6. In the Render shell run python manage.py createsuperuser to create your live admin account.
  7. On Vercel, import the repository with root directory frontend and set API_URL=https://<render-address>/api, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://<your-site>, NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_URL=https://<render-address>/django-admin/.
  8. Open the live site, log in, and add your content in the live Content manager.
Important: Content you add on your computer stays in your local database. The live site has its own database, so add your real content there (or move the database across).
